summary: Root-cause re-derivation confirmed the controller's two supervisor order defects, then found a deeper accepted-contract contradiction that prevents a safe in-scope product patch. The current authority signs an exact whole-root pre-reset observation while a real daemon is live; the required graceful quiesce later deletes daemon control files and checkpoints/closes SQLite, so the child must fail exact observation revalidation before snapshot. A one-stage run-bound IPC handoff cannot satisfy both the fixed lock/header→quiesce→snapshot order and exact restore authority. The incomplete handoff draft was removed; Alembic remains clean at 43306622 with no product changes. This round needs controller/Design review of a two-stage quiesced-observation receipt and action-specific old-writer lifecycle before implementation can safely resume.
verification: Real-writer RED before any product edit: npx vitest run test/unit/DaemonSupervisor.test.ts produced 4 intended failures out of 18—strict execute/recover/complete were swallowed by ordinary ready, and restart killed the live writer before child authority.

Source chain: DaemonSupervisor.start currently returns existing.ready before strict classification and otherwise terminates the existing PID before spawning; daemon-server shutdown removes .asd/daemon.json and .asd/daemon.pid, then AppRuntime.shutdown checkpoints WAL and closes the DB.

Exact-observation chain: createStrictPreResetObservation hashes the complete target root; initializeStrictExternalSetupTarget recreates it after external lease/header setup and rejects any canonical mismatch.
Built dist probe changed only daemon.json/daemon.pid and produced rootTreeChanged=true plus observationChanged=true, with distinct before/after canonical hashes.

Clean-baseline verification after removing the draft: focused DaemonSupervisor + StrictExternalSetupRecovery suite passed 2 files / 26 tests; git status is empty; HEAD/tree remain 43306622a06e2782381aa1aa257681f1f7aa8781 / 13cd8b3c6b1eb80d035750989c849cda53c80a9d.
Alembic Code Guard was attempted on the four owning source files and failed only because the plugin emitted an unrecognized _meta key.
risks: No product commit was created: a minimal one-stage handoff would deterministically violate the existing exact pre-reset observation after legitimate daemon shutdown.

Controller/Design must define whether the accepted authority becomes two-stage, which quiesce-induced target changes are authorized, whether volatile daemon control files belong in snapshot/restore, and how execute/recover/complete resume or replace the old writer.

Alembic project Prime/work/Guard remain degraded because the installed MCP response contains a rejected _meta key; raw source, executable RED/probe evidence, focused tests, and clean Git state were used instead.

craftEvidence.value: Reproduce ready-writer dispatch order, derive the smallest run-bound IPC handoff, then reject it unless graceful writer quiescence preserves the currently signed whole-root observation.
craftEvidence.verify: The investigation stopped at the first deeper contract contradiction before product implementation.

Temporary real-OS-writer RED produced 4 intended failures: restart=false execute did not spawn, recover/complete returned ordinary ready, and restart=true killed the writer before child authority. The temporary tests were removed after the deeper contract blocker was proven.

A built-artifact probe created an exact pre-reset observation, removed only .asd/daemon.json and .asd/daemon.pid as the real shutdown handler does, and observed rootTreeChanged=true and observationChanged=true (before sha256:1d0538383c2cb2c75e99a21618b986d18c6d920857ea45a7eb7ec2e13353695f; after sha256:c8878d8228984c1ac7c9bb5cbbbc2f9e44e726c8d31f019c76edf0e079600884).

craftEvidence.value: The controller-identified order bug is real, but the current rebuild authority contract makes its proposed one-stage repair unsafe. StrictSetupAuthorityReceiptV1 signs a preResetObservation whose rootTreeHash includes every target file. The replacement child must re-create that exact observation after the existing writer is quiesced. Real daemon quiescence deletes daemon.json/daemon.pid and performs a WAL checkpoint/close, so a graceful quiesce necessarily changes the signed root before snapshot. Moving termination behind a run-bound authority message therefore only shifts the failure to STRICT_SETUP_PRE_RESET_OBSERVATION_MISMATCH. SIGSTOP/SIGKILL or ignoring the hash cannot prove SQLite transaction/lock safety or exact recovery. A controller/Design decision is required for a two-stage contract: external authority + lease + durable header, authenticated graceful quiesce, then a durable quiesced-observation receipt bound to the original authority and explicitly governed volatile/control-file and execute/recover/complete resume semantics.

craftEvidence.verify: After removing the incomplete draft, 2 files / 26 tests passed on the exact clean baseline.

craftEvidence.value: Stage 1 checked the dispatch objective against the fixed R0 order and exact-observation recovery guarantees. Stage 2 rejected one-stage IPC, premature graceful termination, strong-signal freezing, stale control-file snapshotting, and hash exclusion as either deterministically failing or outside the accepted safety contract.
No product or test files remain changed; no AlembicCore, AlembicAgent, AlembicPlugin, Test, Design, Wakeflow, vendor, or Ghost root was modified.
